goalForm.createSubtitle: Define your investment goal using the SMART framework

step1.title: What's your goal?
step1.subtitle: Be specific about what you want to achieve. A clear goal is the first step to success.
step1.titlePlaceholder: e.g., House down payment, Emergency fund, Dream vacation
step1.titleError: Please enter a goal title (at least 3 characters)
step1.descriptionPlaceholder: Describe your goal in detail. What exactly do you want to achieve? The more specific, the better.
step1.descriptionError: Please be specific about your goal (at least 20 characters)
step1.smartTipText: Instead of "save money", try "Save $50,000 for a down payment on a 3-bedroom house in Austin". Specific goals are easier to plan and track.

step2.title: Set your target
step2.subtitle: How much do you need to achieve this goal?
step2.amountError: Please enter a valid amount greater than 0
step2.smartTipText: Giving your goal a specific dollar amount makes it real. You can't track progress towards "saving some money", but you can track progress towards $10,000.

step3.title: When do you need it?
step3.subtitle: Set a realistic deadline. A goal without a date is just a dream.
step3.dateError: Please select a date in the future
step3.smartTipText: A deadline creates a sense of urgency and helps you calculate exactly how much you need to save each month to reach your goal.

step4.title: Categorize your goal
step4.subtitle: Which bucket does this goal fit into? This helps determine the right investment strategy.
step4.smartTipText: Different goals require different investment strategies. Safety goals need low risk. Growth goals balance risk and reward. Dream goals can afford higher risk.

step5.title: Why does this matter?
step5.subtitle: Connect your goal to an emotional anchor. This is what will keep you going when saving gets tough.
step5.whyPlaceholder: e.g., I want to provide financial security for my family, or I want to have the freedom to travel the world.
step5.smartTipText: A relevant goal matters to you and aligns with your other relevant goals. If the goal isn't important, you won't stick to it.
step5.example1: To have peace of mind knowing I can handle unexpected expenses.
step5.example2: To build a legacy for my children and their education.
step5.example3: To enjoy my retirement years without financial stress.
step5.example4: To have the freedom to pursue my passion projects.

threeBucket.title: The 3-Bucket Execution Playbook
threeBucket.subtitle: Allocate your income across Safety, Growth, and Dream buckets for balanced progress.

step1.title: Calculate your monthly savings capacity
step1.description: Review your income and expenses to determine how much you can set aside each month.

step2.title: Fund Safety first
step2.description: Direct at least 50% of your savings toward Safety bucket goals until they are fully funded.

step3.title: Split the rest between Growth and Dream
step3.description: Allocate remaining savings: roughly 30% to Growth goals and 20% to Dream goals.

step4.title: Rebalance quarterly
step4.description: Every 3 months, review your allocation and shift funds as goals are completed or priorities change.

snowball.title: Snowball Method
snowball.subtitle: Focus on your smallest goal first, then roll savings into the next one for momentum.

step1.title: List all goals by amount (smallest first)
step1.description: Sort your goals from the smallest target amount to the largest.

step2.title: Put all extra savings into the smallest goal
step2.description: Make minimum contributions to other goals, but throw everything extra at the smallest one.

step3.title: Complete and celebrate
step3.description: When the smallest goal is reached, mark it complete and celebrate the win.

step4.title: Roll forward to the next goal
step4.description: Take the full amount you were saving and add it to the next smallest goal. Repeat.

avalanche.title: Avalanche Method
avalanche.subtitle: Prioritize the highest-importance goals first to maximize impact.

step1.title: Rank goals by importance and urgency
step1.description: Order your goals by which ones matter most or have the nearest deadlines.

step2.title: Allocate maximum savings to the top goal
step2.description: Direct the bulk of your savings to the highest-priority goal while maintaining minimums elsewhere.

step3.title: Monitor deadlines closely
step3.description: Track progress against target dates and adjust contributions if you fall behind.

step4.title: Cascade savings downward
step4.description: Once the top goal is funded, redirect all savings to the next highest-priority goal.

automate.title: Automate Your Savings
automate.subtitle: Pay yourself first with automatic transfers so saving happens without thinking.

step1.title: Open dedicated accounts for each goal
step1.description: Create separate savings or investment accounts for your top goals to avoid mixing funds.

step2.title: Set up automatic transfers on payday
step2.description: Schedule recurring transfers from your checking account the same day you get paid.

step3.title: Start small, then increase
step3.description: Begin with an amount that feels comfortable, then raise it by 1-2% each month.

step4.title: Review and adjust annually
step4.description: Once a year, review your automatic transfers and increase them in line with income changes.

setbacks.title: Handling Setbacks
setbacks.subtitle: What to do when you miss a month or face an unexpected expense.

step1.title: Don't panic or abandon the goal
step1.description: Missing a month is normal. One skipped contribution won't derail a long-term plan.

step2.title: Recalculate your monthly target
step2.description: Spread the missed amount across remaining months instead of trying to make it up at once.

step3.title: Trim non-essential spending temporarily
step3.description: Look for short-term cuts (eating out, subscriptions) to get back on track faster.

step4.title: Adjust the timeline if needed
step4.description: If catching up isn't realistic, extend your target date rather than increasing stress.

monthlyReview.title: Monthly Money Meeting
monthlyReview.subtitle: A 30-minute monthly review to stay on top of all your goals.

step1.title: Log into your dashboard
step1.description: Open FinGoal and review the progress of each active goal against its target.

step2.title: Record check-ins for each goal
step2.description: Update the current saved amount for every goal to keep your progress chart accurate.

step3.title: Review upcoming deadlines
step3.description: Check the timeline view for any goals approaching their target date and assess if you are on track.

step4.title: Set next month's action items
step4.description: Decide if any contributions need adjusting and note any upcoming large expenses that could impact savings.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: FinGoal is committed to protecting your privacy. This policy explains what data we collect, why we collect it, and how you can control it.

localData.heading: Your Goal Data (Local Only)
localData.body: All financial goals you create are stored exclusively in your browser's localStorage. This data never leaves your device and is not transmitted to any server.

analytics.heading: Anonymous Analytics
analytics.body: If you consent, we collect anonymous page view data via Vercel Analytics. This includes pages visited and general usage patterns. No personally identifiable information (PII) is collected. Analytics can be declined using the consent banner.

howWeUse.title: How We Use Data
howWeUse.body: Your local goal data is used solely to display your goals within the application. Anonymous analytics data (when consented) is used to understand which features are most useful so we can improve the product.

dataSharing.title: Data Sharing
dataSharing.body: We do not sell, trade, or share your personal data with third parties. Anonymous analytics data is processed by Vercel, whose privacy policy is available at vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy.

retention.title: Data Retention & Deletion
retention.body: Your goal data is stored in your browser until you clear it. To delete all your data, clear your browser's localStorage for this site (browser Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data). Your analytics consent preference is also stored in localStorage and can be reset in the same way.

yourRights.title: Your Rights
yourRights.body: You have the right to access, correct, or delete your data at any time. Since all data is stored locally in your browser, you have full control. You may withdraw analytics consent at any time by clearing localStorage.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For privacy-related questions, please open an issue on our GitHub repository.
